source.label: thm:batch-bandit-fullinfo
source.quote: Let Algorithm~\ref{alg:batch-partition} be run with batch size $b \ge \frac{\dmax}{C-1}$. Then, with learning rates $\alpha_{\tau} = \sqrt{1/\tau}, \beta_{\tau} = \sqrt{\frac{\log(K)}{D_{\tau}^b}}$, the regret in the bandit regime satisfies: $\eR_T \le 14\sqrt{TbK} + 3\sqrt{D\log(K)}$.

results.notes: Regret defined as E[sum l_{t,A_t}] - min_i sum l_{t,i} against oblivious adversary.

source.label: thm:batch-bandit-fullinfo
source.quote: In the full-information regime, with learning rate $\beta_{\tau} = \sqrt{\frac{\log(K)}{\tau + D_{\tau}^b}}$: $\eR_T \le 12\sqrt{Tb\log(K)} + 3\sqrt{D\log(K)}$.

symbols.C_cap: capacity (max number of simultaneously tracked rounds)

source.label: thm:fixed-delays
source.quote: Consider Delay Scheduling with fixed delays $d_t = d$. Across all scheduling frameworks regardless of preemptibility and clairvoyance, the minimax regret is $\Theta(\sqrt{TK(1+d/C)} + \sqrt{Td\log(K)})$ for the bandit regime and $\Theta(\sqrt{T(d+1)\log(K)})$ for the full-information regime.

results.notes: Upper half of the Theta statement; via Theorem 3.1. Paper's fixed delay d mapped to canonical D. Lower half recorded from Theorem D.5 (requires K <= floor(CT/(d+1))).
Upper half of Theta; holds for any capacity C (optimal capacity Theta(1)). Proof uses b = max{1, ceil(d/(C-1))}, implicitly C >= 2.

conditions: holds even with clairvoyance and preemption

source.label: thm:fixed-delays-lb
source.quote: For $K \le \tfloor{\frac{CT}{d+1}}$ in the bandit regime, the minimax regret of Delay Scheduling with fixed delays is of the order $\Omega\rbr{\sqrt{TK (1+\tfrac{d}{C})} + \sqrt{Td\log(K)}}$.

results.notes: Reduction from label-efficient bandits (Audibert-Bubeck) and delayed bandits (Cesa-Bianchi et al.).

source.label: thm:fixed-delays-lb
source.quote: And for arbitrary $K$ in the full-information regime, regret is of the order $\Omega\rbr{\sqrt{T(d+1)\log(K)}}$.

symbols.nu_T: normalizer 2*H_T, H_T the T-th harmonic number
symbols.delta: overflow probability in (0,1) satisfying the overflow condition

source.label: thm:CNP-results
source.quote: Let $\cS$ be Scheduler~\ref{alg:scheduler-bernoulli} with probabilities $p_t = \min\{1, \frac{C}{(1+\alpha)\nu_t}\cdot \frac{1}{d_t+1}\}$ such that $\alpha$ satisfies \eqref{eq:chernoff-condition} for some $\delta \in (0,1)$. Then, in the bandit regime, ... $\eR_T \le 4\sqrt{K} \sqrt{T + \tfrac{(1+\alpha)\nu_{T}}{C} (D + T)} + 3\sqrt{D \log(K)} + \delta T.$

results.notes: With C >= 3 log T, alpha = 1, delta = T^{-1/2} gives O(sqrt(TK + log(T)/C (D+T)K) + sqrt(D log K)) (Table 2). With alpha = e T^{0.5/C} - 1 for general C (Table 5).

source.label: thm:CNP-results
source.quote: And in the full-information regime, with learning rate $\beta_t = \sqrt{\frac{\log(K)}{\sum_{s\in [t]} (\mu_s + d_s)}}$: $$ \eR_T \le 3\sqrt{\log(K)}\sqrt{(D + T)(1+\tfrac{(1+\alpha)\nu_T}{C})} + \delta T.$$

symbols.d_max: known upper bound on maximum delay

tuning: Pareto proxy delays with scale C/((1+alpha)nu_t), shape 1
alpha_t, beta_t as in Theorem 5.2 using observed z_s and C*mu_max,t

source.label: thm:NCP-results
source.quote: Let $\cS$ be Scheduler~\ref{alg:scheduler-proxy-delays} with parameter $\alpha$ satisfying \eqref{eq:chernoff-condition} for some $\delta \in (0,1)$. Then, in the bandit regime, ... $\eR_T \le 4\sqrt{K} \sqrt{T + \tfrac{(1+\alpha)\nu_{T}}{C} (D + T)} + 3\sqrt{D\log(K)} + 7\sqrt{C \mu_{\max}(K\mu_{\max} + \log(K)\dmax)} + \delta T.$

results.notes: mu_max involves nu_T, so learning rates use mu_max,t (anytime). With C>=3log T, alpha=1: adds O~(d_max sqrt(1+K/C)) (Table 3).

source.label: thm:NCP-results
source.quote: And in the full-information regime, ... $\eR_T \le 3\sqrt{\log(K)} \sqrt{(D + T)(1+\tfrac{(1+\alpha)\nu_T}{C})} + 3\sqrt{C\mu_{\max}\log(K)(\mu_{\max} + \dmax)} + \delta T.$

source.label: cor:NCNP-known-TD
source.quote: In the bandit regime, suppose $C\le \tfrac{D+T}{\sqrt{TK}}$. Setting parameters as ... the algorithm in Theorem~\ref{thm:NCNP-fixed-p} achieves a regret bound of $\eR_T \le 4\sqrt[3]{\tfrac{T(D+T)K}{C}} + 2\sqrt{(D+T)\log(K)}$.

results.notes: Capacity restriction ensures p<=1; larger capacity can simulate smaller.

source.label: cor:NCNP-known-dmax
source.quote: Suppose $C \ge 2$ and $\dmax > 0$. Algorithm~\ref{alg:batch-partition} with batch size $b = \tceil{\tfrac{\dmax}{C-1}}$ and learning rates from Theorem~\ref{thm:batch-bandit-fullinfo} guarantees that $\eR_{T} \le 28\sqrt{\tfrac{T \dmax K}{C-1}} + 3\sqrt{D\log(K)}$ in the bandit regime

source.label: thm:expected-capacity-lb
source.quote: Suppose $\Cexp \ge \tfrac{(d+1)K}{T}$. Then, in the bandit regime, the minimax regret of Delay Scheduling with fixed delays under the expectation-capacity constraint is of the order $\Omega\rbr{\sqrt{TK (1+\tfrac{d+1}{\Cexp})} + \sqrt{Td\log(K)}}$.

source.label: thm:expected-capacity-lb
source.quote: And in the full-information regime, regret is of the order $\Omega\rbr{\sqrt{(1+\tfrac{1}{\Cexp})T(d+1)\log(K)}}$.

results.notes: Theorem's assumption C_E >= (d+1)K/T stated for the whole theorem; applied here too.
